old_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a body of water, likely a lake or pond, reflecting the surrounding trees and sky. The water is very still, with only a slow, diffuse movement of mist or steam rising from its surface. The reflection of the trees is visible, showing pale tones at the top and dark silhouettes on the right, suggesting early morning or late evening light. The sky above is overcast, with a soft, diffused light that enhances the tranquil atmosphere. There are no visible animals or characters in the frame, focusing entirely on the natural elements. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to take in the peaceful and reflective nature of the scene.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a body of water, likely a lake or pond, reflecting the surrounding trees and sky. The water is calm, with gentle ripples moving across its surface, suggesting a light breeze. The reflection of the trees is prominent, showing a mix of green and orange foliage, indicating a change in seasons, possibly autumn. The sky above is overcast, with a soft, diffused light that enhances the tranquil atmosphere. There are no visible animals or characters in the frame, focusing entirely on the natural elements. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to take in the peaceful and reflective nature of the scene. The subtle movement of the water and the changing reflections create a dynamic yet calming visual experience.
caption: The video captures a near-still, misty water surface viewed from above, its plane mirroring the surrounding foliage. An orange-brown leafy canopy is reflected across the top, dark-green trees line the right edge, and a broad pale-gray reflection fills the center, with two pale vertical marks at the lower-left. Throughout the excerpt, gentle ripples continuously wobble and deform these reflected shapes rather than the objects themselves. The canopy reflection at the top shifts and breaks up slightly frame to frame, while the green tree reflections on the right ripple and distort. A tiny bright speck sits near the middle of the frame, drifting only a few pixels with minor jitter and never traveling across the surface. The two lower-left marks remain fixed, changing only in slight blur as the water moves. No large-scale translation occurs, and the overall layout of reflections stays preserved.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
